notes: Identity assessed independently from the repository cover and manuscript title page: matching title, all six authors, journal/volume/pages/year and DOI 10.1016/j.evolhumbehav.2014.02.004. Document is identified as an Accepted Manuscript and contains abstract, Methods, Results, Discussion, references, tables and figures (manuscript pp. 1–29); this is a primary report, not an abstract-only parse. No PDF was supplied. Only locator is "p. 5"; study and description are null. Manuscript p. 5 is introduction, not target statistics. No mapping from published-paper page 5 to manuscript pages is documented in the supplied text. Multiple study/outcome/test candidates remain; requested Cohen's d alone cannot select the target. Candidate Study 2a intimacy attention versus no attention: n=29 participants after excluding one suspicion case, t27 = 5.91, p < .001, d = 2.20 (pp. 14–15). Candidate Study 2b intimacy attention versus no intention: n=44 participants after excluding one suspicion case, t42 = 4.10, p < .001, d = 1.27 (pp. 15–16). Candidate Study 2b interest in friendship contrast: same study participant count 44, t42 = 1.96, p = .057, d = 0.59 (p. 16). Candidate Study 2c intimacy omnibus: n=36 after excluding two suspicion cases, F2, 33 = 3.97, p = .028, η2 = .194 (pp. 16–17); its pairwise tests report p = .055 and p = .048 with no d there. Earlier Studies 1a/1b contain additional ANOVA and mediation tests (pp. 9–11), so candidates are not an exclusive target list. No effect-size conversion or N arithmetic performed. All candidates retained for target resolution; none promoted to row-specific positive values. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
